item.title: Broken slabs, 6th October
item.description:
I am writing to report an urgent health and safety and safeguarding concern regarding the broken/damaged paving slabs on the green. The slabs appear to have been vandalised/damaged by children playing in the area, leaving broken pieces of stone/slab that can potentially cause injury or be picked up and thrown. There is a clear risk that children playing around the damaged area could trip, fall or cut themselves on the broken slabs and exposed edges. The situation has also already resulted in a stone being thrown at a neighbouring resident’s window. Fortunately, nobody was injured, but this could easily have resulted in a serious injury had someone been struck. There is also the potential for significant financial damage if a window were to be broken. Given the risks to the children using the green, neighbouring residents and surrounding properties, I believe this should now be treated as a safeguarding and health and safety issue requiring urgent action, rather than simply general maintenance. I would therefore ask the Council to arrange for the damaged/broken slabs to be?removed and replaced as soon as possible and for the area to be made safe in the interim. Consideration should also be given to whether any further measures are necessary to prevent children from accessing loose or broken pieces of material and potentially injuring themselves or others. Please could you confirm that this matter has been formally logged and advise when the necessary remedial works are expected to be undertaken. Given the potential for further injury or damage, I would appreciate this being treated as a matter of urgency.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): 69, Place Farm Avenue, Crofton, Greater London
Report on FixMyStreet
